import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/training_6.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# According to operation_history, perform UNION of all source tables
# All source tables have the same schema: ['nombre', 'n_concursados', 'n_aprobados', 'año']
# So we can concatenate them directly

union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the target schema and types:
# Target Schema: ['nombre': string, 'n_concursados': integer, 'n_aprobados': integer, 'año': integer]

# Convert columns to correct types
union_df['nombre'] = union_df['nombre'].astype(str)
union_df['n_concursados'] = union_df['n_concursados'].astype(int)
union_df['n_aprobados'] = union_df['n_aprobados'].astype(int)
union_df['año'] = union_df['año'].astype(int)

# Save the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_41/target_multisource.csv"
union_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
